$comment: Mach-O DYNAMIC LIBRARY (MH_DYLIB, .dylib) for ARM64 Darwin/macOS (Apple Silicon) -- c153, the D-LK3-3 anchor (plan 14 / roadmap A3): the Mach-O mirror of the c150 ELF .so + c152 PE .dll. Consumed by `src/link/format/macho.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine: `macho.filetype = dylib` routes UNCONDITIONALLY through the SAME `encodeExecDynamic` substrate the exec image uses (even with zero externs -- the export trie needs the dynamic arm), with the dylib divergences: mach_header filetype MH_DYLIB (6) + no MH_PIE, NO __PAGEZERO (base-0 image dyld slides at load -- `image.pageZeroSize` = 0 and __TEXT.vmaddr = 0), NO LC_LOAD_DYLINKER (mapped by the already-running dyld), NO LC_MAIN (a dylib has no process entry; validate() rejects the entry cluster here exactly as the ELF dyn + PE dll schemas do), an LC_ID_DYLIB carrying `image.installName`, the EXPORT TRIE in LC_DYLD_INFO_ONLY.export_off (every externally-visible defined function + data global, real prefix-compressed radix nodes dlsym walks), real-named nlist entries for externally-visible functions, internal absolute data slots (fn-ptr tables / &global initializers / relro rows) REBASE-opcoded so dyld adds the load slide (the ELF R_X86_64_RELATIVE mirror), extern-targeted data slots emitted as SYMBOL-BASED dyld BIND opcodes with the slot zeroed (D-LK-IMAGE-DATA-SLOT-EXTERN-ADDR Mach-O half -- the ELF c150 symbol-based-Rela mirror; never the baked got-slot/stub address), and an ad-hoc code signature with execSegFlags = 0 (NOT CS_EXECSEG_MAIN_BINARY -- codesign ground truth for a non-main image; Apple Silicon refuses to dlopen unsigned native code, so DSS self-signs). The macOS loader consumes the output: `dlopen("./libdss.dylib") + dlsym("dss_add")` on Apple Silicon. Differs from macho64-arm64-darwin-exec.format.json in: `macho.filetype` (dylib vs execute), `macho.flags` 0x100085 = MH_NOUNDEFS|MH_DYLDLINK|MH_TWOLEVEL|MH_NO_REEXPORTED_DYLIBS (the ld64 dylib convention -- NO MH_PIE, an executable-only flag; NO_REEXPORTED_DYLIBS is safe: DSS emits no LC_REEXPORT_DYLIB), `image.pageZeroSize` 0, NO `image.dylinkerPath`, NEW `image.installName`, text `virtualAddress` = segmentPageSize (base-0 image by construction -- validate() pins the equality, the ELF dyn text-VA==pageAlign mirror), NO `entryPoint`/`processExit`/`entryCallingConvention`/`processArgs`, `tlsAccess` + tdata/tbss rows OPTED IN 2026-08-19 (cycle P12): the dlopen TLV path is MEASURED on real Apple Silicon and dylib thread-locals work through the SAME per-image TLV descriptors the exec uses (D-LK3-DYLIB-TLS-MODEL, CLOSED -- see $tlsAccessComment), NO `librarySynthesis` (the pthread <threads.h> shim inside a dylib is an untested form -- the c152 dll precedent), and `artifactProfiles` ["lib"].
$stackReserveUnsupportedReasonComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: a shared library carries an image header but NO field for a stack size (there is no LC_MAIN in a MH_DYLIB / no stack-size field in an ELF ET_DYN), and a loaded library never owns a thread's stack anyway, so a `stackReserve` / `--stack-reserve` request is REFUSED with an actionable remedy rather than silently dropped.
$dataModelComment: Same LP64 identity as the exec sibling (64-bit Darwin).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: macOS ships on APFS/HFS+ volumes that are CASE-INSENSITIVE by default (the installer default since 10.13; a case-sensitive volume is opt-in), and Apple's own SDK headers rely on it -- `<TargetConditionals.h>` / `<CoreFoundation/CoreFoundation.h>` are routinely spelled with divergent case. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component rather than delegating to fs::exists, so a Darwin cross-build from a case-sensitive Linux host resolves exactly as it does natively.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: Apple's C ABI prefixes EVERY C symbol with exactly ONE leading underscore, on both 32- and 64-bit Mach-O -- the rule has no bitness axis and no per-arch axis (the arm64 and x86_64 slices of the universal libSystem decorate identically), which is why it is declared per FORMAT and not per target. EVIDENCE, EACH LABELLED. MEASURED-BY-EXECUTION (recorded TF-C113, the macOS cross-build arc): a Windows host cross-emitted a mach-o arm64 binary whose only process-exit path is the `_exit` import, and it RAN on the operator's Apple Silicon Mac and exited correctly -- an undecorated `exit` would have been an unresolved dyld bind, not a cosmetic difference. MEASURED (recorded TF-C121): libSystem's x86_64 slice exports BOTH `_fstat` and `_fstat$INODE64`, i.e. the C identifier `fstat` reaches the linker as `_fstat`. NOT RE-MEASURED THIS CYCLE, stated rather than buried: the Mac is a personal machine and was not declared reachable, so nothing here rests on a probe taken today. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$cCallingConventionComment: D-FFI-ABI-CATALOG-SELECTS-CALLING-CONVENTION-BY-FORMAT-IDENTITY: the platform C ABI for code compiled into this format, NAMING a row in the paired target's callingConventions[] array. Apple's ARM64 ABI — NOT `aapcs64`: it packs named stack arguments naturally, always stacks variadic arguments, and reserves x29 unconditionally (`framePointerReservation: always` on that row). Every one of those divergences lives on the cc row this name selects, so selecting the right name is what makes them apply.
$outputExtensionComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the extension the driver appends to an artifact this format produces. This used to be derived in C++ by `program/target_spec.cpp::outputExtensionFor`, a five-arm `switch (fmt.kind())` with a NESTED per-flavor switch inside each arm -- seven identity mentions computing a NAMING fact, which is not an engine behaviour at all. The nest existed because one ObjectFormatKind spans several artifact flavors; a DOCUMENT is exactly one flavor, so the whole derivation collapses to this one string. REQUIRED on every format. An EMPTY value is a DECLARED answer and not an omission -- a Unix executable carries no extension -- which is why the in-memory field is an `optional` and the loader's required check asks `contains`, never `empty`.
$archiveFlavorComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: WHICH `ar` variant this format's ECOSYSTEM uses. Declared on every native format, not only the `container: archive` ones, because that is what the deleted C++ derivation answered: `(format.kind() == ObjectFormatKind::Pe) ? Coff : SysV` was handed WHATEVER format the caller had, and `linkAndWriteStaticArchive` is reachable with the RELOCATABLE format of an ecosystem as well as its archive one (MEASURED -- restricting the key to archives reddened link/test_ar_writer and program/test_static_link). NOT cosmetic: the coff flavor carries the little-endian second linker member link.exe requires to resolve members at all. A closed VERB rather than an open name, because an archive layout is an ENGINE capability -- only variants `writeArArchive` realizes can be honored.
$targetArchComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the .target.json NAME this format is for. `crossValidateTargetFormat` compares it against TargetSchema::name() -- two DECLARED NAMES -- where it used to run a six-arm `switch (format.kind())` reading a DIFFERENT field per identity (elf.machine / pe.machine / macho.cputype) and compare each against a hardcoded C++ table, kTargetArchMachineCodes, keyed on (target name x format kind). THAT TABLE IS DELETED, and the argument is ONE OWNER rather than tidiness: `arm64 is EM_AARCH64 = 183` had two owners -- this document's own machine field and that C++ row -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the identical shape as kCManglingRules and kAbiCatalog. The number now lives only in the document that emits it, and the pairing question is answered by a name this document states outright. Adding a new arch is now JSON-ONLY.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): the C-visible face of this file's `dataModel` above, DERIVED FROM THAT VALUE AND NEVER FROM THIS FILE'S NAME -- the loader synthesizes no macro name and the engine performs no format-identity branch; it merges whatever rows are declared here with the language's `preprocess.predefinedMacros` and the target's `predefinedMacros`, applying `availableObjectFormats` exactly once. DECLARED ON THE FORMAT because the data model is per-(OS x format), not per-CPU: the same x86_64 target is LP64 here and LLP64 under pe64-x86_64-windows-*, so a target-side row would be wrong on one of its own formats -- which is exactly what both .target.json files say when they record `__LP64__`/`_LP64` as DELIBERATELY NOT SHIPPED and defer to the format. BOTH spellings, each value 1: MEASURED 2026-07-30 with `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target <triple>` (Apple clang 21.0.0), __LP64__ and _LP64 are BOTH defined as 1 on arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, aarch64-linux-gnu and x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, and NEITHER is defined on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc. COLLISION POLICY: a name declared by this file AND the language or target config is FATAL (C_ConflictingPredefinedMacro) -- no side silently wins. WHAT IT UNBLOCKS, MEASURED: the macOS SDK gates 234 occurrences across 91 headers on __LP64__, so without these rows DSS compiled the SDK's ILP32 arms while its own widths were LP64 (sizeof(long)==8), and $SDK/usr/include/mach/port.h:113-114 then asserted the user32 struct size 12 instead of user64's 16 -- sqlite mem1.c's three error[S0029]. RED-ON-DISABLE: delete this key and examples/c/predefined_lp64_macho stops exiting 42.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: Apple arm64 == generic AAPCS64 == gnu_packed, same as the exec sibling. ~~ CORRECTED P45 (D-CSUBSET-ZERO-WIDTH-BITFIELD-ALIGNMENT): the sentence above claiming Apple's arm64 divergences do NOT include bit-field allocation is MEASURED FALSE, and it is why the divergence went unmodelled. Apple DOES diverge on the alignment an UNNAMED bit-field contributes -- `struct { char c; unsigned :0; char d; }` is 5/1 on Apple arm64 and Apple x86_64 but 8/4 on generic AAPCS64 ELF (MEASURED: Apple clang 21.0.0 on the physical macOS host; gcc 13.3.0 + clang 18.1.3 per target). The PACKING claim the sentence was really making stands -- gnu_packed is still the right strategy here -- but the ALIGNMENT half is now carried by the separate `unnamedBitFieldAlignment` key below, which this document declares as `ignored`. A $comment asserting a settled answer gets probed LESS than a claim in code, which is the whole reason this correction is written in place rather than left to the next reader to re-derive.
$unnamedBitFieldAlignmentComment: D-CSUBSET-ZERO-WIDTH-BITFIELD-ALIGNMENT: an UNNAMED bit-field contributes NO alignment to the enclosing composite. MEASURED P45 -- `struct { char c; unsigned :0; char d; }` is 5/1 here, against 8/4 on the AAPCS64 ELF formats that share this very same `gnu_packed` strategy. ~ THIS IS AN APPLE DIVERGENCE FROM GENERIC AAPCS64, and this document's own `$bitFieldStrategyComment` asserted the opposite until P45. MEASURED on the physical macOS host with Apple clang 21.0.0 via `/usr/bin/clang -arch arm64`, rc=0. The zero-width field still BREAKS the packing cursor to its declared type's unit boundary (uncapped by `#pragma pack`); only the alignment contribution is dropped. ~ Declared on the FORMAT and not the target for exactly the reason `bitFieldStrategy` is: one CPU target serves several ABIs. There is NO target-side fallback for this key -- omitting it does not inherit, it leaves the axis undeclared and the layout engine fails loud the moment a zero-width bit-field needs it.
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: Apple arm64 `long double` IS `double` (IEEE binary64) -- the same value macho64-arm64-darwin-exec, macho64-arm64-darwin and macho64-arm64-darwin-staticlib already declare, and the same row tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp `ShippedFormatsDeclareTheAbiTruthTable` pins as 'apple arm64 = f64'. ADDED 2026-08-06 by the format-family sibling-symmetry sweep, which is the whole point of that test: this was the ONLY arm64 Darwin format missing the axis, and nothing had noticed because no arm64-dylib corpus uses `long double`. MEASURED, red -> green: before this key, `long double widen(double d){ return (long double)d + 1.0L; }` was REJECTED here with `error[S0056] ... got 'long double ' is not realized on this object format: the format declares no longDoubleFormat axis`, while the identical source compiled at rc=0 on macho64-arm64-darwin-exec and macho64-arm64-darwin. A .dylib and a .o built from the SAME translation unit therefore disagreed about whether the type exists. NOT a bulk copy from a sibling FILE: the value is the Apple arm64 ABI fact (long double is a synonym for double on Apple silicon), which is why every other arm64 Darwin format independently says `f64` -- and why the x86_64 dylib says `x87-80` instead. ⚠ The x86_64 dylib's `$longDoubleFormatComment` claims 'arm64 macOS uses IEEE-128 and omits this field'; that sentence is WRONG on both halves and is corrected there in the same commit.
$externCallDispatchComment: Same call-site shape as the exec image: the walker synthesizes a __stubs entry per extern FUNCTION (ADRP+LDR+BR x16 through the __got slot, dyld-bound eagerly) and the call site is a plain direct BL to the stub -- pc-relative, so the code needs no fixup under the dylib load slide. D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH.
$dataImportBindingComment: c153 (D-LK3-3 + D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT): extern library DATA objects bind via Mach-O __got non-lazy pointers exactly as on the exec image (the import machinery is dyld's, not the artifact flavor's -- the c152 PE precedent): the walker reserves a __got slot per imported object, the bind stream names the symbol + owning dylib ordinal, dyld writes the object's address at load, and the c117 GotIndirect lowering (lea-of-slot + deref) reads it.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: rodata (read-only __TEXT,__const -- reloc-FREE items only: a reloc-bearing const item routes to relro at the producer, and a hand-built reloc-bearing rodata item fails loud at the walker's __const rebase guard), data (mutable initialized globals, __DATA,__data), bss (zero-init, __DATA,__bss S_ZEROFILL), relro (reloc-bearing CONST data, c145 -- merged into __data by the image arm so its rebase/bind slots land in dyld-writable pages, the same fold the exec makes). tdata/tbss: OPTED IN 2026-08-19 (cycle P12, D-LK3-DYLIB-TLS-MODEL) -- the dlopen TLV path is now MEASURED on real Apple Silicon (see $tlsAccessComment); the linker's pre-walker gate admits thread-local items exactly as the exec arm does.
$tlsAccessComment: D-LK3-DYLIB-TLS-MODEL closed 2026-08-19 (cycle P12): the `macho-tlv` model, IDENTICAL to the exec sibling's (see that file's $tlsAccessComment for the descriptor-call access sequence and the writer machinery -- all shared). The open question this row existed for was whether dyld's TLV setup runs for a dlopen'd (vs launch-time) image and how threads existing BEFORE the dlopen observe the new image's thread-locals. MEASURED on real Apple Silicon (arm64, macOS 26.5.2, a clang-built TLV dylib + dlopen client, probe in the cycle's artifact log): a WORKER thread dlopen'ing the image reads its own instance (bump 7->8) and the MAIN thread -- alive before the load -- observes a FRESH, INITIALIZED instance (initial 7, bump 8). Mach-O TLV descriptors are per-image (each image carries its own __thread_vars and dyld rewires at image load), so NO dylib-specific access machinery exists to declare: the exec's model IS the dylib's model. The format-level declaration is what un-gates the MIR->LIR access lowering and the linker's section gate for the `lib` artifact profile.
$artifactProfilesComment: This format SERVES the shared-library profile (plan 06 AP3), mirroring elf64-x86_64-linux-dyn + pe64-x86_64-windows-dll. The cli profile is NOT served (a .dylib is not a runnable console binary). ★ `module` JOINED THIS SET 2026-08-15 (plan 06 §5.1 B.12, as CORRECTED): a module IS a library, so it is served by every format that serves `lib` or `staticlib` and by nothing else. `artifactProfile` says what a project builds ITSELF as; `DependencyComposition` says how it is CONSUMED (`module` is SourceMerge — a consumer takes its SOURCES and ignores its artifact). Those are orthogonal, so a module builds standalone like any other library and the static-vs-dynamic choice is made by the `<target>:<format>` spec the author writes in `targets[]`, exactly as it already is for `lib` vs `staticlib` — no new rule and no engine change.

macho.$comment: mach_header_64 identity. cputype = CPU_TYPE_ARM64 = (12 | CPU_ARCH_ABI64 0x01000000) = 0x0100000C = 16777228; cpusubtype = CPU_SUBTYPE_ARM64_ALL (0) -- same silicon as the exec sibling. filetype = 'dylib' (MH_DYLIB = 6). flags = MH_NOUNDEFS (0x1) | MH_DYLDLINK (0x4) | MH_TWOLEVEL (0x80) | MH_NO_REEXPORTED_DYLIBS (0x100000) = 0x100085 = 1048709 -- the ld64 dylib convention: NOUNDEFS because every undefined is bind-resolved, TWOLEVEL is the modern namespace (each bind names a specific dylib ordinal), NO_REEXPORTED_DYLIBS tells dyld it need not chase re-exports (DSS emits no LC_REEXPORT_DYLIB). MH_PIE is deliberately ABSENT -- it is an executable-only flag (a dylib is inherently position-independent; dyld slides its base-0 image unconditionally).

image.$comment: Mach-O image fields for MH_DYLIB. pageZeroSize = 0 -- a dylib carries NO __PAGEZERO (validate() enforces; ld64 likewise rejects -pagezero_size on non-main links): __TEXT.vmaddr = 0 and dyld slides the whole base-0 image to its load address. segmentPageSize = 16384 (0x4000) -- Apple Silicon requires 16 KiB-aligned segments, same as the exec. NO dylinkerPath (LC_LOAD_DYLINKER is a main-executable load command). installName = the LC_ID_DYLIB identity a CLIENT records at link time ('@rpath/...' is the modern convention); plain dlopen-by-path ignores it. Like `codeSignature.identifier` below, a shipped-schema default identity is a deliberate concession -- a differently-named artifact overrides via its own format JSON (the walker NEVER derives it from the output file name; c150 DT_SONAME discipline). loadDylibs = [libSystem] -- the home of any libc import this dylib's code makes (every ld64-produced dylib depends on libSystem; harmless when unused since libSystem is loaded in every macOS process anyway). bindNow = true (eager binding, the v1 stance). buildVersion macos 11.0 -- dyld wants a platform load command on modern macOS for libraries too (ld64 always emits one). codeSignature = ad-hoc SHA-256: Apple Silicon REQUIRES all native code signed -- dlopen of an unsigned arm64 dylib fails with a code-signature error, so DSS self-signs exactly as the exec does; the walker sets CodeDirectory execSegFlags = 0 for this flavor (NOT CS_EXECSEG_MAIN_BINARY -- `codesign -s -` ground truth for a non-main image). codeSignature.identifier is the CodeDirectory identity (kernel keys the signature on it; generic shipped default, same concession as installName).

$staticInitializersComment:
D-C-GNU-CONSTRUCTOR-ATTRIBUTE-IS-WARNED-AND-IGNORED-NOT-RUN: THIS FORMAT DECLARES NO STATIC-INITIALIZER RUNNER, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE ANSWER -- recorded so nobody 'completes' the key by adding one.
A dylib is an IMAGE but not an EXEC flavor: `isExecFlavor()` is false, so DSS injects no entry trampoline and there is no synthesized entry to call anything. `imageLoader` would be the truthful arm -- dyld really does run a `__mod_init_func` section in a dylib -- but it requires a WRITER that emits one typed S_MOD_INIT_FUNC_POINTERS, and no DSS writer emits any static-initializer section today. Declaring either arm would therefore be false. With nothing declared, the linker REFUSES a program that schedules an initializer for this format, naming the format and the remedy -- which beats an initializer that silently never runs.

sections.$comment: __text within __TEXT. virtualAddress = 0x4000 = image.segmentPageSize -- the base-0 dylib layout: page 0 holds the mach header + load commands, __text opens page 1 (textFileOff = alignUp(headerAndCmds, segmentPageSize) = 0x4000 while the load commands stay under one page -- the walker's congruence guard fails loud if they ever grow past it), and validate() PINS virtualAddress == segmentPageSize (the ELF dyn text-VA==pageAlign mirror; dyld slides everything by the load base). flags (substrate `type`) = S_REGULAR | S_ATTR_PURE_INSTRUCTIONS (0x80000000) | S_ATTR_SOME_INSTRUCTIONS (0x400) = 0x80000400, same as the exec sibling.
sections.name: __text

sections.$comment: __const within __TEXT -- read-only data globals (reloc-free; the exec sibling's row verbatim). virtualAddress = 0 -- walker-computed (H1-aligned after __stubs). addrAlign = 8 is the schema FLOOR; the walker raises it to the strictest item's alignment.
sections.name: __const

sections.$comment: __data within __DATA -- writable initialized globals (D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER); relro rows fold in here with their dyld rebase/bind sites (c145 + c153). virtualAddress = 0 -- walker-computed.
sections.name: __data

sections.$comment: __bss within __DATA -- zero-init globals. `type` (section_64.flags) = S_ZEROFILL (1): VM extent, no file bytes, LAST section in __DATA. virtualAddress = 0 -- walker-computed.
sections.name: __bss

sections.$comment: D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL (TLS C4): __thread_data within __DATA — the INITIALIZED thread-local TEMPLATE (`thread_local int g = 7;`). `type` (section_64.flags) = S_THREAD_LOCAL_REGULAR = 0x11 = 17: dyld COPIES this section's bytes into every thread's freshly-allocated TLS block (the per-thread initial image). File-backed (contributes __DATA file bytes). It is the LOW address of the per-thread TLV template region [__thread_data, __thread_bss-end); each descriptor's word2 (offset) is measured from here (CRIT-2, 0-based). addrAlign=1 is the FLOOR (member-driven, gcc/ld64 parity — a larger floor would inflate every thread's block); the walker H1-raises it to the strictest thread-local's alignment (capped at 16 by the over-align gate). virtualAddress=0 — walker-computed after __data.
sections.name: __thread_data

sections.$comment: D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL (TLS C4): __thread_bss within __DATA — the ZERO-INIT thread-local TEMPLATE extent (`static thread_local int c;`). `type` (section_64.flags) = S_THREAD_LOCAL_ZEROFILL = 0x12 = 18: like S_ZEROFILL it occupies VM but stores NO file bytes (section_64.offset=0; excluded from __DATA.filesize) and MUST follow __thread_data CONTIGUOUSLY so the TLV region is one span (dyld calloc's the block, so the zero-fill tail reads 0 in every thread). addrAlign=1 FLOOR (H1-raised, <=16). virtualAddress=0 — walker places it at __thread_data-VA + alignUp(tdataSpan, tbssAlign) so a tbss var's descriptor offset is block-relative. reuses the shared isZeroFill predicate.
sections.name: __thread_bss

sections.$comment: D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL (TLS C4): __thread_vars within __DATA — the thread-local variable DESCRIPTORS. `type` (section_64.flags) = S_THREAD_LOCAL_VARIABLES = 0x13 = 19. Each 24-byte `tlv_descriptor` = { word0 thunk (a bind to the undefined libSystem `__tlv_bootstrap`; dyld overwrites it with its tlv_get_addr at load), word1 key (0; dyld fills the pthread key), word2 offset (the variable's 0-based offset into the [__thread_data,__thread_bss] block) }. WRITER-synthesized (not AssembledData) — the writer mints one per thread-local and stores symbolVa[sym]=descriptorVA so the access adrp/add resolves here (F3). File-backed. addrAlign=8 (three u64 words). entrySize could be 24 but the writer emits it as 0 (matching __got's table convention). virtualAddress=0 — walker-computed; the descriptors are NOT part of the per-thread copied template.
sections.name: __thread_vars

relocations.$comment: ARM64 Mach-O relocation kinds -- the exec sibling's table verbatim (`kind` MUST match arm64.target.json's rows; nativeId is descriptive on image flavors, which apply relocs in place). ARM64_RELOC_BRANCH26 = 2, length 2, pcrel 1 -> 0x25000000. ★ `isCall` (D-LK-MACHO-ISDATA-NO-CALL-SIGNAL, 2026-08-20): this wire relocation can ONLY target executable code, so an object reader that meets an undefined extern through it has PROVEN the extern is a function rather than a data object -- the only classification signal a symbol-name-only reference offers. It is declared HERE, on the format row, and not derived from the target's formula, because a formula describes ARITHMETIC and not ROLE: `S + A - P` is the identical arithmetic for a call and for a PC-relative data reference, so the x86_64 target's `linear` is honest and simply carries no role, while aarch64's `aarch64_call26` looked like a role only because that CPU's branch has its own instruction encoding. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-20: every macho64-x86_64 archive member calling any library function was unreadable for exactly this reason while the arm64 sibling read the same source cleanly. The target document cannot carry it -- it is PER-CPU and shared with ELF, where the same `rel32` genuinely serves data references too.
relocations.name: ARM64_RELOC_BRANCH26

relocations.$comment: ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED = 0, length 3 (8 bytes), pcrel 0 -> 0x06000000. abs64 -- legal in DATA items only on this arm: an internal target gets a REBASE opcode (dyld adds the slide); an extern target gets a symbol-based BIND opcode with the slot zeroed (D-LK-IMAGE-DATA-SLOT-EXTERN-ADDR).
relocations.name: ARM64_RELOC_UNSIGNED
